query: How can businesses improve Yelp user satisfaction?

per_column.name: service_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Directly targets the query on improving satisfaction by categorizing service failures; a strong axis to group actionable problems. Samples are well grounded: 'ignored_forgotten' matches being forgotten twice, 'rude_dismissive' matches discriminatory refusal, positive reviews correctly 'not_present'.

per_column.name: pricing_value_perception
per_column.rationale: Value perception is a distinct, actionable lever for satisfaction. Mostly grounded, though YLP-0003's 'overpriced_for_quality' is a slight stretch (reviewer notes portion-size/pricing suggestion, not overpricing for quality); acceptable warranted inference. Positive/silent rows handled well.

per_column.name: staff_conduct_severity
per_column.rationale: An ordinal severity scale enables modeling/ranking of staff issues, complementing the categorical issue type rather than duplicating it. Values are plausible readings (praise=1, forgotten-twice=4, discriminatory=3), but the scale is somewhat subjective and NULL vs 1 handling is inconsistent, introducing mild grounding uncertainty.

per_column.name: business_category
per_column.rationale: Provides a genuine grouping dimension to compare satisfaction drivers across business types. Samples are sound: grill/pizza=restaurant, cabana/drinks venue=nightclub_bar, real-estate professional=other. Some categories require inference but are warranted from text cues.

judge.rationale: All four columns give distinct, non-redundant analytical axes (issue type, pricing perception, severity, business segment) directly serving the satisfaction-improvement query. Values are generally sound readings of the source text with correct 'not_present' handling for silent/positive rows; only mild subjectivity in the severity scale and one borderline pricing label slightly reduce groundedness. No clear hallucinations observed.
